'''Spartak Timofeyevich Belyaev''' (October 27, 1923 – January 5, 2017) was a Soviet and Russian theoretical physicist who was awarded a [[Lomonosov Gold Medal]].<ref name=russkiymir>{{cite web|url= http://www.russkiymir.ru/en/news/125395/|title=Russian Academy of Sciences Award Lomonosov Medal to Spartak Belyaev and Gerard 't Hooft|publisher=[[Russkiy Mir Foundation]]|date=May 17, 2011|accessdate=April 20, 2015}}</ref>

==Biography==
Belyaev was born on October 27, 1923, in [[Moscow]], Russia. When World War II began, he graduated from high school and by August 1941 enlisted himself into the Army as a volunteer. During that time he participated in various battles in [[Caucasus]] and liberation of Poland in 1945. After long years of war, he declined the offer on keeping the career and instead decided to become a physicist by applying to the [[Moscow State University]]. 

Two years later he already got a job there as a researcher at the Atomic Energy Institute which later on was renamed as [[Kurchatov Institute]]. He worked there till 1962 and between that year and 1958 also worked at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] in [[Copenhagen]]. That year Belyaev generalized [[Nikolay Bogolyubov]]'s theory of the [[weakly interacting Bose gas]] using [[quantum field theory]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Shuryak |first=Edward |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Quantum_Many_Body_Physics_in_a_Nutshell/CKtuDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=belyaev+weakly+interacting+bose+gas&pg=PA46&printsec=frontcover |title=Quantum Many-Body Physics in a Nutshell |date=2018-11-27 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-18496-8 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Belyaev |first=Spartak |date=1958 |title=Energy spectrum of a non-ideal Bose gas |journal=JETP |volume=34 |issue=2 |pages=299}}</ref>

In 1962 he decided to change his lifestyle a bit; he moved to [[Siberia]] and in 1968 was elected as a full member of [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. He worked at the [[Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics]]. For his breakthroughs and research in physics he was awarded the [[Landau Gold Medal]] in 1998 and the [[Feenberg medal]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Vladimir Zelevinsky|title=Spartak T. Belyaev — Recipient of the Feenberg medal|journal=[[International Journal of Modern Physics]]|volume=20|issue=2574|pages = 2574–2578|year=2006|doi=10.1142/S0217979206035047|bibcode = 2006IJMPB..20.2574Z |author-link = Vladimir Zelevinsky}}</ref> 

On May 17, 2011, he and [[Gerard 't Hooft]] were awarded a Lomonosov Gold Medal by the Russian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="russkiymir" />
